title: The History of Tekken | From the 1994 Arcade to Tekken 8
description: How Tekken grew from a 1994 Namco arcade game into one of the biggest fighting game series: Tekken 3, the PlayStation years, Tekken 7, a Guinness World Record and Tekken 8 in 2024.

sections.heading: The King of Iron Fist
sections.script: Tekken means iron fist in Japanese, and for more than thirty years it has been one of the most famous fighting game series in the world. It started in arcades, grew up on the PlayStation, and today it is played on PlayStation 5, Xbox and PC. Its story follows the Mishima family and the King of Iron Fist Tournament, and Guinness World Records has even recognised its long running story. In this video we go through the history of Tekken, from the first game in nineteen ninety four, through the classics like Tekken 3, to the arrival of Tekken 8. Tekken has always been closely linked with PlayStation, with its arcade games running on hardware based on the PlayStation, so its story is also part of PlayStation history. Get ready, because the fight is about to begin.

sections.heading: Nineteen ninety four: the first Tekken
sections.script: The first Tekken was made by Namco and appeared in arcades in nineteen ninety four. Guinness World Records says it was unleashed in arcade halls on December ninth, nineteen ninety four. It was one of the first fighting games to use three dimensional characters. The PlayStation version launched in early nineteen ninety five in Japan and in the fall elsewhere, and it set a new high mark for home ports, because the arcade hardware was very similar to the console. Players loved the four button control scheme, where each button controls one limb, and it is still the heart of the series.

sections.heading: Tekken 2 and the family drama
sections.script: Tekken 2 arrived in arcades in late nineteen ninety five and on PlayStation in nineteen ninety six. It shifted the story's focus to Heihachi Mishima, the previous villain, and added new fighters such as Jun and Lei, along with a long list of characters that you could unlock over time, so players kept coming back. The home version brought modes that became series staples, like Team Battle, Time Attack, Survival and Practice, and a beautiful computer graphics intro movie. It also set the tone for the series: serious fights, a dramatic family rivalry, and cutscenes that fans enjoyed watching as much as playing.

sections.heading: Tekken 3 changes everything
sections.script: For many fans, Tekken 3 was where it all began. It came out in arcades in nineteen ninety seven and on PlayStation in nineteen ninety eight. The story moved ahead about twenty years, and it introduced Jin Kazama, who became a lead hero, together with Hwoarang, Bryan, Eddy Gordo and Ling Xiaoyu. All characters could now sidestep into the screen, which made the three dimensional arenas feel alive. The PlayStation version added Tekken Force, a side scrolling action mode, and Tekken Ball, a famous party mode, plus the series' first guest character, a tiny dinosaur named Gon. It sold more than eight million copies on PlayStation and is still often called one of the best fighting games ever made. It was even one of twenty games included on the PlayStation Classic mini console in twenty eighteen.

sections.heading: The PlayStation 2 years
sections.script: When the PlayStation 2 arrived, Tekken was ready. Tekken Tag Tournament came to the console in the year two thousand, with much better visuals than the arcade version, and let you build a team of two fighters and swap between them during a match. Its huge roster brought in characters from across the series. Tekken 4 followed in two thousand one in arcades, with a big change: arenas with uneven ground, walls and obstacles that you could use in battle. It also pushed the story more, with a full story mode on the home version. Tekken 5 then arrived in two thousand four and added character customization with cosmetic items.

sections.heading: Tekken 5 and Tekken 6
sections.script: Tekken 5 became a fan favourite, and its updated version, Dark Resurrection, came to the PlayStation Portable in two thousand six, bringing the series to a handheld. Tekken 6 reached arcades in two thousand seven, and an update, Bloodline Rebellion, followed in late two thousand eight. The home version, released in two thousand nine on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, was the first time Tekken appeared on more than one console brand. It added the Rage system, where a fighter with low health deals more damage, a large Scenario Campaign story mode, and arenas with breakable walls and floors. It kept the series fresh for a new generation.

sections.heading: Tag teams and free to play
sections.script: After Tekken 6, the series tried some new ideas. In twenty eleven, Tekken Hybrid bundled an HD remaster of Tekken Tag Tournament with the computer animated film Tekken Blood Vengeance. Tekken Tag Tournament 2 also reached arcades in twenty eleven, and a console version followed in late twenty twelve with a huge roster of characters from across the series. A free-to-play version called Tekken Revolution also arrived, letting players earn in-game currency to unlock fighters, and it ran until twenty seventeen. These experiments kept the community active during the years between the numbered games, and they prepared the series for a return to its roots with a new numbered entry.

sections.heading: Tekken 7 and the guests
sections.script: Tekken 7 reached arcades on March eighteenth, twenty fifteen, and an updated version, Fated Retribution, followed in July twenty sixteen with a famous guest, Akuma from Street Fighter. The game came to PlayStation 4, Xbox One and PC on June second, twenty seventeen, and it received years of updates. Surprise guests included Geese Howard from Fatal Fury, Noctis from Final Fantasy fifteen and Negan from The Walking Dead. Tekken 7 was a huge success, and it has sold twelve million copies, which makes it the best selling game in the series. The console version also included a long story mode that continued the Mishima saga.

sections.heading: Guinness World Records
sections.script: In twenty seventeen, Guinness World Records honoured Tekken with two titles. The series was recognised for the longest running videogame storyline without any substantial development gaps or reboots, since its story has unfolded in order from one game to the next. It was also recognised as the longest running three dimensional fighting game franchise, stretching for twenty one years and one hundred seventy nine days at that time. Series director Katsuhiro Harada collected the certificates, and he said he was never aiming to become number one, just like the fighters in the story, who focus on beating their rivals one at a time.

sections.heading: Tekken 8
sections.script: Tekken 8 launched on January twenty sixth, twenty twenty four, on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and PC, and it did not come to the older consoles. Its story mode, The Dark Awakens, focuses on the final confrontation between Jin Kazama and Kazuya Mishima. It introduced the Heat system, which rewards aggressive play, and it supports cross-platform play between the PlayStation 5, Xbox and PC versions. Bandai Namco said it sold more than one million copies on its first day and more than two million in its first month, which was faster than Tekken 7, and by early twenty twenty five it had passed three million. Season 2 of its downloadable content began in early twenty twenty five with new fighters, and the Tekken World Tour esports circuit returned the same year, giving fans around the world a stage to compete on.

sections.heading: Your favourite fighter
sections.script: That is the story of Tekken, from an arcade cabinet in nineteen ninety four to a global series with a world record to its name. Now we want to hear from you. Which Tekken game is your favourite: the original, Tekken 3, Tekken 7 or Tekken 8? And who is your main character: Jin, Kazuya, Heihachi, Paul, King or someone else? Tell us in the comments below, and subscribe to the channel for more gaming history, news and guides.
